{\large\bf Proof of a conjecture of Abdollahi-Akbari-Maimani
concerning the non-commutative graph of finite groups
\footnotetext[2]{This work was partially supported by CONACYT.}
Luis A. Dupont, Daniel G. Mendoza and Armando S\'anchez-Nungaray
The non--commuting graph $\Gamma(G)$ of a non--abelian group $G$ is defined as follows. The vertex set $V(\Gamma(G))$
of $\Gamma(G)$ is $G\setminus Z(G)$ where $Z(G)$ denotes the center of $G$ and two vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent
if and only if $xy\neq yx$. For non--abelian finite groups $G$ and $H$ it is conjectured that if $\Gamma(G) \cong \Gamma(H)$, then $|G|=|H|$.
